races.name: Dunbrody Beginners Chase

runners_data.name: Impero
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old with a solid record on Good ground (10 wins/places from 15 similar-going runs) but a natural front-runner who will find the prominent berths congested in this field, forcing him to race in a less comfortable mid-pack position; Ben Harvey and Cian Collins are a lesser-profile combination than rivals here, and the redistribution makes his chance harder to assess at face value.

runners_data.name: Nadia's Boy
runners_data.note: Mullins-trained six-year-old with two wins from three starts on Good ground and an impressive 1/110 hurdles form sequence suggesting real class for this level; Brian Hayes takes over and he has won three of his five chase starts — his natural desire to race prominently will be tested by the busy early exchanges, and 61 days off is a minor query, but his raw ability makes him live at any early price.

runners_data.name: Scalpnagoon
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy's mount for Gordon Elliott arrives in good form (three seconds from his last four completions) and handles Good ground well, but like Impero he is a prominent type who may find himself shuffled back by the sheer number of horses seeking that ground; the tongue-strap is noted, and his best form has come over slightly longer trips — the 2m here is on the sharp side for him.

runners_data.name: Soir De Garde
runners_data.note: The eight-year-old is the most natural fit for the dominant race shape: a genuine prominent racer with a win and a second on Good ground from limited similar-going starts, trained by Mullins who is firing at 26% over 14 days; his form string (1/2FP-) includes a fall and a pulled-up run that need explaining, but his underlying class on Good ground makes him a key player if he settles into his rhythm.

runners_data.name: Wendrock
runners_data.note: The sole true hold-up horse in the race, trained by Gordon Elliott and ridden by Danny Gilligan, but his recent figures (45P0-4) paint a picture of a horse that is struggling to deliver; he benefits from the prospect of being covered up early, but in a race likely run at a controlled pace, the lack of a true end-to-end gallop means he will need something to go wrong up front rather than finishing on merit — the headgear (hood for the first time in this context) is worth monitoring.

runners_data.name: William Tell
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner from David Harry Kelly's yard, with two wins on Good and Soft from front-running positions and clear experience dictating a race; Cian Quirke takes the ride and the STYLE_FIT tag (0.91) reflects that his best form came at longer trips (22f wins) making 2m potentially on the sharp side, but his role as sole pacesetter is the defining tactical factor in this race and he should not be crowded early.

races.paceDynamic: William Tell is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, he should secure a comfortable, uncontested gallop from the front over this 2m Wexford trip on Good ground. The pace will be honest but controlled — a beginners' chase over 2m on Good ground with a solo leader almost always produces a rhythm that suits the prominent-to-front profile rather than those who need a strong pace to close into. Nadia's Boy, Impero, and Scalpnagoon are all natural prominent racers, but with William Tell and Soir De Garde also seeking that territory, there is simply not enough room at the head of affairs for all of them — the most likely beneficiaries of the front positions after William Tell are Soir De Garde (proven prominent) and whichever of Nadia's Boy or Scalpnagoon secures early cover. This race shape — a steady-to-honest gallop set by one controlled front-runner — strongly favours horses who can travel prominently without expending energy fighting for position, making the prominent-to-lead profile the primary beneficiary and rendering true hold-up tactics largely redundant.

scenarios.title: William Tell Controls Wire-To-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If William Tell gets his customary uncontested lead and dictates an honest but sustainable gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: If William Tell gets his customary uncontested lead and dictates an honest but sustainable gallop throughout.

scenarios.title: Prominent Chaser Wears Him Down
scenarios.trigger: If William Tell sets a pace that is just quick enough to compromise his stamina late, allowing a well-placed chaser to reel him in at the last.
scenarios.body: If William Tell sets a pace that is just quick enough to compromise his stamina late, allowing a well-placed chaser to reel him in at the last.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Scrappy Early Pace Bunches Field
scenarios.trigger: If the cluster of promoted prominent types jostle for position early, creating a messy gallop that compresses the field and brings closers back into play.
scenarios.body: If the cluster of promoted prominent types jostle for position early, creating a messy gallop that compresses the field and brings closers back into play.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Errors Cost Leader; Class Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If William Tell makes a significant jumping error mid-race that disrupts his rhythm and allows a classier rival to stride past.
scenarios.body: If William Tell makes a significant jumping error mid-race that disrupts his rhythm and allows a classier rival to stride past.

watchPoints.text: William Tell (headgear flagged) — monitor his jumping in the early fences; any significant blunder or loss of confidence at a fence will immediately release the chasing pack and transform the race shape entirely.

The opening half-mile could see three or four horses all angling for prominent positions — Nadia's Boy, Scalpnagoon, Impero and Soir De Garde all want to race forward, and a tight, bumpy start over fences at Wexford can cause interference or unwanted jumping errors before the field settles.

Soir De Garde's unfinished form (form string includes F and P) means his jumping under pressure is a live risk; if he makes a mistake at a critical fence while travelling well, he could cost himself a winning chance from an otherwise ideal position.

Nadia's Boy has been off 61 days — watch the paddock for signs of fitness and how quickly Brian Hayes positions him in the first few fences; if he drops back rather than travelling prominently, his chance is materially reduced given this pace map.

Wendrock's hood headgear is noted — if the early pace is genuinely messy and the race bunches, watch whether Danny Gilligan can produce him with a run between the last two fences, as that is his only viable winning move given he cannot manufacture his own pace in this race shape.

races.name: Tintern Trails Handicap Chase

runners_data.name: An Peann Dearg
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner on OR 123, Paul Nolan yard at 0/14 in the last fortnight, but this 9-year-old has solid recent Good-ground form (sim-going 11/15) and is a genuine hold-up horse who will need a true pace to deliver his run from off the bridle.|

runners_data.name: Trasna Na Pairce
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner; De Bromhead in form at 11/38 T14 and the mare's course record features two Good-ground placings — she is however racing out of her natural role (STYLE_FIT 0.92) as she is essentially a prominent-to-lead type rather than a pure front-runner by preference.|

runners_data.name: Ma Belle Etoile
runners_data.note: 320 days off the track is the main query for this De Bromhead seven-year-old, but her record shows two wins on Good at 16f and a win at 18f — the trip and surface are ideal and she resumes from a long break with fresh conditions squarely in her favour.|

runners_data.name: Mercury Mission
runners_data.note: Consistent placer on Good ground (3W6P in similar conditions), LP McKenna claiming 3lb, and this horse has finished second or third in four of his last five runs at 2m — prominent style suits this track and the going absolutely suits.|

runners_data.name: Solsbury Hill
runners_data.note: 186 days since last run for this Conor O'Dwyer-trained six-year-old, and the last run was a blank (0 finish) — however his OR-114 mark, a win on Good at 16f and Good-ground sim figures (10/13) suggest he retains ability if bouncing back fresh.|

runners_data.name: Femme Magnifique
runners_data.note: Returned to winning form last time (1/16f/GOO, OR 111) and trainer David Harry Kelly is in sharp form at 2/3 T14 — a prominent-style mare who is ideally drawn for this sharp 2m on ground she handles well.|

runners_data.name: Jane Eire
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse (hg:ht) with a consistent run of Good-ground efforts for De Bromhead, 30 days since last run alongside stablemates — she will need the pace to develop honestly and clear air on the bend to produce her best.|

runners_data.name: Be Fierce
runners_data.note: 9-year-old with tongue-tie, Good-ground record reads 1W2P in similar conditions (sim-going 11/15), and four consecutive finishes of 4th or better suggest consistent form — a prominent runner who rarely wins but rarely falls out of the frame.|

runners_data.name: Party President
runners_data.note: Young claimer Dylan O'Connor (7lb) aboard, and the form string (2/16f/SOF most recent win) shows he handles cut better than pure Good — hold-up style and a patchy Good-ground record (sim-going 6/12, 2W3P) makes this ground slightly borderline.|

runners_data.name: Presenting Lad
runners_data.note: 10-year-old with a strong Good-ground profile (sim-going 13/15, 1W4P) but at OR 103 carries bottom weight for a reason — a true hold-up type whose preferred rear-of-field position has been displaced, meaning he faces working from further forward than natural.|

runners_data.name: Tequila Talkin'
runners_data.note: Paul Nolan's seven-year-old is a natural prominent racer who finds himself mapped to midfield in a field with too much early pace — STYLE_FIT 0.92 tempers his chance, though his last run (2/16f/GOO) confirms he retains winning form on this ground.|

runners_data.name: That's About Right
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse (hg:tp) operating off a lowly OR 102, shuffled to midfield because rear positions are oversubscribed — his Good-ground sim figures are mixed (sim-going 12/15, 2W5P over longer trips) and the sharp 2m is shorter than ideal.|

runners_data.name: Mic Drop
runners_data.note: Won last time at 18f on Good (1/18f/GOO, OR 101) under Josh Williamson (5lb claim) and is a natural prominent horse who will have to work to recover his preferred position — his class is proven but the redistribution to midfield is a genuine tactical disadvantage.|

races.paceDynamic: Trasna Na Pairce is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner handicap chase over 2m at Wexford, and with no rival expected to seriously contest the early lead, she should be able to dictate a sustainable, controlled gallop on Good ground. Behind her, Ma Belle Etoile, Mercury Mission, Femme Magnifique and Be Fierce are natural prominent racers who will press to track closely, creating a well-strung-out chasing group rather than a burning pace. The field contains significantly more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate — Tequila Talkin', Mic Drop and Presenting Lad are all natural pace horses redistributed to midfield, with Ma Belle Etoile, Mercury Mission and Femme Magnifique most likely to actually secure prominent positions. A controlled, single-paced gallop from Trasna Na Pairce with a close-order chasing group favours horses who can race handily from the second or third fence — prominent, on-pace runners who avoid traffic on this sharp track will have the clearest route to the line, making the prominent profile the dominant beneficiary of this race shape.

scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Disruptors Capitalise

scenarios.body: If redistribution chaos — too many prominent types crowding the early stages — creates scrimmaging that fragments the field and hands an advantage to the horses mapped centrally.

watchPoints.text: Ma Belle Etoile returns from 320 days off the track — watch her in the parade ring and early in the race for any signs of rustiness, as a stale run would remove the most dangerous prominent rival from the equation.|

The cluster of prominent types — Ma Belle Etoile, Mercury Mission, Femme Magnifique and Be Fierce — will all seek the same early berths behind Trasna Na Pairce; watch the first two fences for crowding or interference that could compromise one or more of their runs.|

Tequila Talkin' and Mic Drop are natural pace horses forced off the front rank — watch whether either jockey attempts to push forward early regardless, which could ignite the gallop and undermine the controlled scenario entirely.|

An Peann Dearg (top OR at 123) is 54 days since last run and Paul Nolan's yard is at 0/14 in the last fortnight — watch his pre-race market move as a guide to whether connections believe he is spot-on for this assignment.|

Trasna Na Pairce's jumping fluency is critical — she is the race's sole pace-maker and any fencing error, particularly at the open ditch, would collapse the tempo structure and create an unpredictable scenario from that point forward.|

races.name: Duncannon Beach Handicap Chase (0-100)

runners_data.name: Shannon Bank
runners_data.note: Won at Wexford last time out over this exact course and distance on Good ground; Sean O'Keeffe retains the ride and Andrew Kinirons' yard is 0/8 in the past 14 days but the form profile here is the strongest in the race; front-runner who is very much in his element.

runners_data.name: Figurehead
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse with a poor recent run sequence including a pulled-up effort and two finishes outside the top ten; handles Good going but hasn't won in this campaign and the 48-day break is worth noting; tongue-tie fitted.

runners_data.name: Miss Oreo
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with a largely disappointing recent profile — pulled up last time out — and while she handles Good ground her form at 16f is unremarkable; Josh Williamson's claim is the main angle, but the yard is 0/16 in a fortnight.

runners_data.name: Tumuch
runners_data.note: Missed 93 days before a 65-day penalty period and returns now as a genuine hold-up type whose best form came over longer trips; Good ground suits on the evidence of prior runs and the Dreaper yard is worth monitoring, but lack of recent racing is a concern.

runners_data.name: Jouster
runners_data.note: Consistent placing profile — three placings from five runs at this distance — and Paul Flynn's yard is 3/22 in the past fortnight which represents positive activity; handles Good ground well and the close-up finishing style should keep him competitive.

runners_data.name: Auntie Lacey
runners_data.note: Natural rear-of-field type whose true instinct is to race from the back, though with so many similar horses in this field she is likely to end up in midfield against her preferred pattern; Paul Nolan's yard is 1/14 recently and her Good-ground form shows consistency without a win; STYLE_FIT discount applies.

runners_data.name: Quinn The Eskimo
runners_data.note: Another Paul Nolan-trained hold-up horse who faces the same positional squeeze as stablemate Auntie Lacey; has one win in the past form string but it came on Heavier ground and Good-going form is moderate; likely to be racing against his natural instinct given field composition.

runners_data.name: Sea Of Doubt
runners_data.note: Won over 18f on Good ground two runs back and finished second most recently, making this a horse with genuine claims; Keith Donoghue is a high-quality booking and Ian Donoghue's yard is 2/20 in 14 days; prefers to sit close to the pace rather than deep hold-up, which suits this race shape well.

runners_data.name: Polly Poppins
runners_data.note: Prominent-going type who should be able to secure a position just behind the leaders in the early stages; placed at 16f on Good ground twice and Michael Kenneally's 5lb claim helps with the weight; no win yet but consistent at this level.

runners_data.name: L'Amiral Fromentin
runners_data.note: Young five-year-old whose natural style is to race from hold-up positions, but the crowded field forces him forward in the race map; Darragh O'Keeffe is a significant jockey engagement and P J Rothwell is in strong form (4/26), though the horse has not won and recent form shows 0 from 9 on Good ground.

runners_data.name: Kingdom Calling
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse that fades in the finish — a concern in any scenario — and while mapped to midfield his natural inclination is to be further back; has not won and the Good-ground record shows a runner who finishes seventh or worse frequently; STYLE_FIT discount applies.

runners_data.name: Benzine
runners_data.note: Another hold-up type carried forward in the map by field congestion, with a fade flag that makes him particularly risky if the pace is honest; best form came when finishing second over 18f on Good ground, so the trip is right, but the finish tendency undermines late-race claims.

runners_data.name: Chosen Shant
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old with two career wins and four placings on Good ground — the most experienced horse in the field — but his hold-up style is genuinely compromised in this field; J J Slevin is a top-level booking and the 22-day turnaround is fine, yet the redistribution from his natural position is a real tactical cost.

runners_data.name: Ahellofaman
runners_data.note: Four-year-old who has shown glimpses in finishing second on Heavy ground but has no wins and a modest Good-ground record (3 runs, 0 wins, 0 places); the Hanlon yard is 0/14 in a fortnight and the 67-day absence adds further caution; his natural hold-up style is constrained by this field.

runners_data.name: Sampoet
runners_data.note: Front-runner who provides the crucial competitive element to Shannon Bank's pace; has not won any of his last four completed starts and the tongue-tie is noted; at OR 93 he is competitive on paper but his recent form string is moderate and he is likely to do more race-shaping than race-winning.

runners_data.name: Sunwalk
runners_data.note: Carries a fade-in-finish flag and returns after an 85-day absence, the longest in the field; has only one placing from five recent runs and the jockey booking is not confirmed (no name listed); Good-ground form is moderate and the redistribution out of his preferred hold-up position further undermines his prospects.

races.paceDynamic: Shannon Bank and Sampoet are the two confirmed front-runners in a 16-runner field, and both are likely to press forward from the off, creating a genuinely contested pace on Good ground over 2m. Shannon Bank won over this course and distance last time out and will be hard to dislodge from the front, while Sampoet has enough natural pace to ensure the leader is never able to completely dictate on his own terms — the gallop will be honest rather than suicidal, but consistent enough to stretch the field. The remainder of the field is dominated by hold-up types, many of whom have been redistributed into midfield on the map because the race shape simply cannot accommodate them all at the rear — Quinn The Eskimo, Auntie Lacey, L'Amiral Fromentin, Kingdom Calling, Benzine, Chosen Shant, Ahellofaman and Sunwalk are all genuine back-of-the-field horses who will be competing for the same ground, meaning the true closers will face traffic and positional compromises throughout. Polly Poppins and Sea Of Doubt are the most likely to secure genuinely prominent positions behind the two leaders, with Figurehead and Jouster also capable of tracking in a useful spot. This race shape — contested pace, compressed midfield, congested closing group — favours horses who can travel prominently or make smooth headway from just off the pace rather than deep hold-up types who rely on a clear late run.

scenarios.body: If the congested midfield and hold-up pack encounters enough interference to open up a late run for one of the genuinely back-of-the-field types.

watchPoints.text: Shannon Bank set the early fractions last time at Wexford and is likely to do so again — watch whether Sampoet pushes hard enough to make this a true test or if Shannon Bank gets an uncontested lead after the first fence.

With eight horses redistributed out of their natural hold-up positions, the midfield could become dangerously congested between fences three and six — watch for interference or horses becoming outpaced and causing traffic issues for closers.

Sea Of Doubt arrives off a second place 16 days ago and is likely to be ridden more prominently than her hold-up tag suggests — watch how Keith Donoghue positions her at the first fence as this could define her chance entirely.

Sampoet is fitted with a hood and returns just 17 days after his last run — watch his early behaviour in the paddock and whether he settles into the front-running role or becomes keen and wastes energy before the race develops.

L'Amiral Fromentin runs for a trainer (P J Rothwell, 4/26 in 14 days) showing notably strong form — watch whether Darragh O'Keeffe attempts to reposition him forward earlier than his natural style would suggest given the competitive market around him.

races.name: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Chase

runners_data.name: Leave In Secret
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner; Thomas Gibney yard out of form (0/6 in 14 days) but the horse's ability to control the tempo at 2m7f on Good is a genuine tactical asset — recent form figures (3467-7) are modest yet the racing-from-the-front role here is uncontested, and Dylan Kidd's claim is a useful weight relief.

runners_data.name: Harbour Highway
runners_data.note: Emmet Mullins runner with strong form credentials at 2m4f-2m6f on Good ground (two wins, three places in similar conditions); sits prominent naturally and should find a comfortable position second or third, giving Alan O'Sullivan a simple tactical decision — the 1P2 recent string at similar trips is encouraging.

runners_data.name: Sammy Smart
runners_data.note: Veteran ten-year-old whose Good-ground form is solid and who typically races prominently; the United (URF) in recent starts is a concern, but the 3/22f/Good effort shows he can stay and compete at this level when things fall right.

runners_data.name: Duty Bound
runners_data.note: 50-day absence is the primary flag here; jumps well and stays the trip (2/24f/Good in hist), and Jordan Canavan's claiming allowance softens the weight burden — prominent style means the break is less of a concern if schooled between runs.

runners_data.name: Riggs
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer at 11 years old; all-Good form record (15/15 in sim-going) shows he handles conditions, but the P8 recent string and consistent finishing position in double figures make it hard to be enthusiastic — needs a true test of stamina to get involved.

runners_data.name: Therellbguddaysyet
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old prominently raced with consistent placed form in similar conditions; nothing flashy in recent figures (6/4-58) but the 5/20f/Good and 4/16f/Good suggest he's always thereabouts before the race heats up at the end.

runners_data.name: Rue Taylor
runners_data.note: Paul Nolan's runner is a natural prominent racer who will find the field too crowded ahead of him — likely to race further back than he'd like; the 14-day trainer strike rate of 1/14 is modest, and recent form (0708-5) offers little encouragement even in a more favourable spot.

runners_data.name: Teenage Kiss
runners_data.note: Won last time out (1/24f/Good) which stands out in this field; genuinely wants to race prominent but the congested front end means Charlie O'Dwyer will have to make do with a midfield slot — that style friction tempers what is otherwise the best recent form in the race.

runners_data.name: Secrecies Of Stone
runners_data.note: Paul Nolan sends this one out in good recent form shape (3/14 in last 14 days for trainer); wants to race handy but is likely pushed back in the pack, and the FP9 recent string including a fall and a pulled-up suggest jumping reliability may be an issue over a longer trip.

runners_data.name: Menas Miracle
runners_data.note: Won last time out at 1/22f/Good which gives him live claims; naturally prominent but will likely find himself mid-division in this race — Josh Williamson is a conditional and the horse's 2W in Good conditions is the main positive angle.

runners_data.name: Bohemian Bay
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse that fades in the finish; hold-up style, no wins or places in similar going (0/6 sim-going), and OR of 84 leaves it with a significant class gap — hard to see a route to involvement at 2m7f on this evidence.

runners_data.name: Malton Groove
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner whose best recent effort was 2/24f/Good — shows the trip suits and the stable (Dermot McLoughlin) hasn't hit form lately (0/14 in 14 days); Malton Groove needs the pace to genuinely test the leaders, which this race shape is unlikely to provide.

races.paceDynamic: Leave In Secret is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with only a single genuine pace-setter, is likely to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 2m7f trip on Good ground — nobody is going to seriously pressure it into going too fast. Harbour Highway, Sammy Smart, Duty Bound and Therellbguddaysyet will push to occupy the prominent positions just behind, creating a compact lead group but not a burning pace. This field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural position: Teenage Kiss, Rue Taylor, Secrecies Of Stone and Menas Miracle are genuine prominent racers who are likely to find themselves shuffled back into midfield against their preference. The resulting race shape — one uncontested leader, a moderate gallop, a bunched chasing pack — strongly favours horses who can sit handy in the first three or four and produce a clean jump at the last; true hold-up closers face the classic problem of a pace that never truly tests the leaders enough to reel them in.

watchPoints.text: Leave In Secret — if it jumps off cleanly and settles without a challenger on its shoulder, it could bowl along at a very comfortable clip and be almost impossible to pass; watch the first three fences to see if any prominent runner actively contests the lead.

Teenage Kiss — won last time out and is the form horse, but watch how far back Charlie O'Dwyer finds himself at the first bend; if it is more than six lengths off the pace by the time they reach the back straight, its chance is materially compromised.

Secrecies Of Stone — has a fall and a pulled-up in recent starts over comparable trips; at 2m7f with a big field over fences, any jumping error in the pack could cause significant interference — flag as a faller/unseater risk to those around it.

Harbour Highway — watch how quickly Alan O'Sullivan moves to track Leave In Secret; if he gets into second or third naturally in the early stages, the market positioning and form profile make this the most obvious on-pace beneficiary if the leader weakens.

Malton Groove — if the pace is genuinely slow in the early stages and the field becomes deeply compressed, Patrick O'Brien (claimer) could find himself with no room to produce his run from off the pace; watch the field order turning for home as a read on whether hold-up types have any chance.

races.name: Cottage Autism Network Mares Beginners Chase

runners_data.name: Aruntothequeen
runners_data.note: Trained by Mrs John Harrington and ridden by Darragh O'Keeffe, she has solid placed form on Good ground (sim-going: 9/13) though her last two runs produced only thirds — a natural prominent racer whose position in the pace map is compressed by the volume of similar types in this field, meaning she may have to be more patient than ideal.

runners_data.name: Beauforts Storm
runners_data.note: The only genuine hold-up runner in the race, which makes her a rare commodity here; a string of modest finishes (U5-772) gives limited confidence though she has shown ability at 16f on Good, and a truly run race is the prerequisite for her getting competitive late.

runners_data.name: Colleen Danu
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 20f on Good for Patrick Foley, which is exactly this trip and surface — her jumping credentials are sound and that winning run gives her a live each-way chance, though being squeezed back from her preferred prominent berth in a crowded pace map is the key risk to her running style translating here.

runners_data.name: Farfromnowhere
runners_data.note: Paul Nolan's mare has 109 days between runs, which warrants monitoring, and her last run was a 21st at Leopardstown on Soft — yet she has a win and a second at this sort of trip on Good, and is a classier horse than that last effort suggests; the layoff and the crowded prominent field are the twin concerns.

runners_data.name: Future Prospect
runners_data.note: Mullins and Brian Hayes is a combination that demands respect, and she won last season on Good ground over shorter — fell on her most recent start and has a question mark over jumping reliability at this level, while her natural prominent style being displaced in this pace map means she may race further back than her best form requires.

runners_data.name: Lady Bluebird
runners_data.note: The oldest runner at nine but has been placed at this course on Good and won over 21f — she is arguably the most versatile of the prominent types and her record (51-263, with wins at 19f and 21f on Good) maps directly onto today's conditions, giving her a legitimate chance of holding a front-rank position naturally.

runners_data.name: Pampar Lady
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's mare has an outstanding record on Good ground (sim-going 13/15) and has won at 18f and 19f, making today's 2m3½f the question — she has run well on both fast and soft surfaces and is one of the few in the field who has genuinely posted placed form at every level of her recent campaign.

runners_data.name: Swing Davis
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's six-year-old is identified as the race's sole confirmed front-runner, and Gilligan will look to use that asset from flag to finish — the concern is she carries a STYLE_FIT flag suggesting racing out of her most effective role, and her recent form of P/PU-5 with no win or place on Good (0W2P in sim-going) makes her pacemaking function more valuable than her winning prospects.

races.paceDynamic: Swing Davis is the confirmed and likely uncontested front-runner here, with Danny Gilligan able to dictate her own fractions over 2m3½f on Good ground at Wexford — a track where an uncontested lead is a genuine asset. With no other confirmed front-runner to challenge her, Swing Davis sets a sustainable, controllable tempo that will not burn off the field early but will keep the race honest enough to prevent a sprint finish from behind. This shape broadly favours horses who can race prominently and travel well through the race, ready to press when Swing Davis is called upon jumping the final fences — a prominent-to-press profile is the primary beneficiary. This field contains significantly more prominent-type runners than the race shape can accommodate: Aruntothequeen, Colleen Danu, Farfromnowhere, Future Prospect, and Lady Bluebird are all natural prominent racers, but with Swing Davis already occupying the lead, only one or two can realistically secure a genuine front-rank position — Lady Bluebird and Pampar Lady, who have shown tactical flexibility, are most likely to sit close to the pace without being completely squeezed out.

watchPoints.text: Colleen Danu's recent Good-ground win over this exact trip makes her the most dangerous horse in the race if she overcomes the positional compromise of being squeezed away from her natural prominent berth.
Monitor Swing Davis in the betting — if she drifts, market confidence in her staying role is collapsing and the race shape becomes more unpredictable for everyone tracking her.

Future Prospect's fall last time out means jumping fluency will be scrutinised at the first fence; any hesitation could see her immediately displaced in a field already fighting for prominent positions.

Farfromnowhere's 109-day absence is the longest in the field — watch her in the paddock and pre-race for signs of freshness or rustiness, as her market move will reflect trainer confidence in her readiness.

With five natural prominent types and only room for two or three at the head of affairs behind Swing Davis, the first two fences will be critical in establishing the race order — crowding or early mistakes could dramatically reshape the race.

races.name: Support The Irish Injured Jockeys Fund Beginners Chase

runners_data.name: Ballyearl
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead runner returning from 337 days off who showed a win and a place from his three Good-ground runs — the layoff is the key risk factor but De Bromhead's yard is in form and this horse profiles as a natural prominent type who should land close to the pace if fit.|

runners_data.name: Drop A Threat
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins horse (3/18 T14) who races from hold-up; five Good-ground runs have produced no wins or places at that level and the 0P0W record in similar going makes him a significant hold-up risk to underdeliver even if the pace sets up for closers.|

runners_data.name: In The Trenches
runners_data.note: Comes into this on the back of a win 16 days ago and has hit the frame in 8 of 15 Good-ground outings — his true nature is forward-going but the surplus of prominent types in this field means he is likely to be further off the pace than suits him, which tempers confidence in his chance.|

runners_data.name: Jetovango
runners_data.note: Flagged as prone to fading in the finish; hold-up horse who has managed only one placed effort from four Good-ground starts and has not run since a pulled-up effort 309 days ago — the combination of jumping unknowns, fitness concerns and a finishing tendency to fade makes this a tough one to support.|

runners_data.name: Juke Hill
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott runner dropped into a beginners chase off an 8/57 trainer strike rate over 14 days — genuine hold-up style whose best run (second) came on Good ground over 22f, but the form string shows inconsistency and his jumping will be under scrutiny on chase debut.|

runners_data.name: Kashchei
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 21f on Good ground 55 days ago; races from hold-up position which is genuinely his style, and his form in similar conditions (7 from 12) includes three placed efforts — patient ride from Ben Harvey will be key.|

runners_data.name: Malbas
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old whose best runs came prominently but who is mapped to midfield given the congestion — recent form of 0 on last run and a limited strike rate (2W4P from 15 Good-ground runs) makes it hard to be positive even if he finds a cleaner passage.|

runners_data.name: Ned In The Park
runners_data.note: Amateur ride for Mr D Doyle off a 25-day break with a win and four places from 12 Good-ground starts — a natural prominent type who is well-placed to hold a position in the first half-dozen and his form at around 20f is consistent.|

runners_data.name: Paul Collins
runners_data.note: Long layoff of 169 days is a concern, and despite a win on Good ground over 22f it came early in his career — recent form string of five consecutive out-of-the-frame finishes makes it hard to build a case, even from a prominent pitch.|

runners_data.name: Rockonliam
runners_data.note: Confirmed lone front-runner with two wins on Good ground and a legitimate jumping profile for this chase debut; assigned a STYLE_FIT flag because his front-running role may expose him late in a 16-runner field, but he controls the race shape entirely from the front.|

runners_data.name: Silver Salute
runners_data.note: Another horse flagged for fading in the finish, racing from hold-up off only a 15-day break — zero wins and zero places from six Good-ground runs is a damaging stat, and the combination of style and finishing profile makes this one of the more vulnerable in the field.|

runners_data.name: Clody Diamond
runners_data.note: Six-year-old for Paul Nolan back after 161 days; headgear noted, only one Good-ground qualifying run from four starts — the lack of any meaningful Good-ground base and the extended layoff create too many unknowns to assess with confidence.|

runners_data.name: Rockstown Girl
runners_data.note: Genuinely a hold-up type in her natural style despite being mapped to midfield — her form is actually excellent with 1W5P from 12 Good-ground runs and a sequence of 1-2-3-3, suggesting consistent placed form if she can get a trouble-free run from off the pace.|

runners_data.name: Sophia Rose
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's second string after In The Trenches; a true front-running/prominent horse who is being squeezed towards midfield by the traffic, which means she is unlikely to race as freely as her form warrants — the STYLE_FIT flag is a real concern here.|

runners_data.name: Listentillitellyea
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old veteran who arrives 17 days fresh; a natural forward-goer whose instinct will be to race up with the pace, but with so many prominent types ahead of him in the queue he faces the same positioning problem as Sophia Rose — form on Good has been modest (0W2P from 10).|

runners_data.name: Burru
runners_data.note: Strong claims based on Good-ground figures (15 from 15 qualifying runs) including a recent win 36 days ago — a prominent-style horse whose jumping record and stamina profile at this trip make him one of the most course-and-distance-consistent horses in the field.|

races.paceDynamic: Rockonliam is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 16-runner beginners chase and, critically, faces no genuine challengers for the early lead — he can dictate a measured, sustainable gallop on Good ground over 2m3½f without ever being pressured into a pace war. Behind him, Ballyearl, Ned In The Park, Paul Collins, Clody Diamond and Burru are all natural prominent types who will look to track him closely, but with In The Trenches, Listentillitellyea, Sophia Rose and Malbas all true prominent/forwardly-placed horses squeezed into midfield positions by the sheer volume of pace-preferring types, the early battle for territory is more congested than the race shape suggests from the front. This field holds materially more front-running and prominent types than the race can accommodate cleanly — Rockonliam will lead unchallenged, but Ballyearl, Ned In The Park and Burru are best placed to actually secure the prominent berths behind him, while the redistributed horses face the likelihood of racing well off their natural rhythm. A controlled, non-pressured gallop set by a single front-runner on Good ground over this trip strongly favours horses who travel prominently with a clean view of the fences and enough stamina to sustain their effort into the closing stages.

watchPoints.text: Rockonliam leads but faces a congested pack immediately behind him — any jumping error at an early fence could be collected by the prominent group tracking closely, creating early casualties in a 16-runner field.|

Ballyearl returns from 337 days off for Henry De Bromhead; watch the market closely as De Bromhead horses returning from long layoffs can arrive ready to run, but a rusty jumper in a big-field beginners chase is a significant risk.|

In The Trenches and Sophia Rose — both true prominent horses likely to be squeezed wide or back from their natural position — watch the early stages to see whether either can force a forward berth, as their chance depends entirely on it.|

Burru's trainer Bernard Martin Crowley runs only two horses in the 14-day window (T14: 1/2) — a small but active yard with a recent winner, and this horse's Good-ground record is the strongest statistical base in the race across all 15 qualifying runs.|

Rockstown Girl is the most reliably consistent form horse in the hold-up group with four consecutive top-three finishes on Good ground — watch where she sits on the final bend as a clean run from the rear could see her finish with purpose.|

races.name: Racing Again July 3rd Rated Novice Chase

runners_data.name: Lawful Ruler
runners_data.note: Has finished placed twice in five recent runs on Good, handles this trip, but naturally wants to race prominently and the crowded front end here means jockey Mr T J Stafford will likely find the horse shuffled back against its wishes — a 71-day break adds a small fitness query on top.

runners_data.name: Chichester Park
runners_data.note: Slevin takes the mount for A J Martin who is 2/8 in the past fortnight; last ran 30 days ago and was second latest, but this horse races prominently by nature and has been placed at the rear of the map solely because the hold-up slots needed filling — treat any hold-up read with scepticism.

runners_data.name: Costacurta
runners_data.note: De Bromhead sends out a horse who has rattled up five consecutive placed efforts on Good or similar, the most consistent profile in the race; genuine prominent runner who should access a clean second or third fence slot and is not fighting his natural position.

runners_data.name: Ephesus
runners_data.note: Form string of 0460-7 in recent chase starts offers little encouragement, and the tongue-tie is noted; sits deepest in the field and would need a major positional shift plus jumping improvement to factor, while a 15-day turnaround for Hogan is quick.

runners_data.name: Garnacho
runners_data.note: Thomas O'Connor (7) rides, with Fahey sending him 31 days fresh; two wins on Good ground and the horse has a recent second at 2m4f, suggesting stamina and going are both fine — a genuine prominent type who should get a forward position in a race where several rivals cannot.

runners_data.name: Howdoyalikeherhome
runners_data.note: Elliott's runner carries a hood and has prior experience at the longer trip on Good, including a second at 2m4f; form of 82PP-4 shows jumping errors are a concern, and the prominent style could make those errors costly near the pace.

runners_data.name: Londonofficecallin
runners_data.note: Donoghue rides a horse who won at 12f on Soft and has placed five times in fifteen Good-ground runs; would naturally want to be handy but the volume of pace in this race pushes Cromwell's runner back — the style displacement at a 15-day turnaround makes this a harder ride.

runners_data.name: Maxi Mac Gold
runners_data.note: Nolan's 7-year-old is on a 67-day break and comes in with headgear (tongue-tie, blinkers); a natural prominent runner who has been mapped rearward because the field is front-heavy, so Alan O'Sullivan (5) will need to settle for a position that does not suit.

runners_data.name: Mister Pink
runners_data.note: Five consecutive finishes in the 4-6 range on Good ground underline a solid but limited profile; naturally races prominently and has been pushed back on the pace map — Doyle will find it hard to manufacture the prominent position this horse needs and the flat form cycle gives no upside angle.

runners_data.name: Reiki Revolution
runners_data.note: Cromwell's confirmed front-runner, returned 22 days ago after two unseated-rider runs; a single win on Good supports the going, and with no real challenger for the lead, Stone-Walsh can dictate — the key risk is whether the jumping errors that produced those URs have been addressed.

races.paceDynamic: Reiki Revolution is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival willing or able to press from the outside, should coast into an uncontested lead at a sustainable Good-ground gallop over 2m3½f at Wexford. The redistribution flags tell the real story: Maxi Mac Gold, Londonofficecallin, Mister Pink, and Lawful Ruler are all natural prominent types who cannot all achieve their preferred berth, meaning several will have to race in unfamiliar midfield positions and expend energy doing so. Costacurta, Garnacho, and Howdoyalikeherhome are genuine prominent horses who will press for the best available slots just behind Reiki Revolution, creating a competitive early order but not a truly searching pace. The tactical verdict is clear: this race shape strongly favours a horse that can sit just off a lone, untroubled leader and produce a clean jumping round with a sustained late effort — a well-positioned prominent or flexible midfield type with good Good-ground form is the profile to follow.

watchPoints.text: Reiki Revolution's jumping — two consecutive unseat-rider exits mean any blunder at a fence in the back straight could bring down several horses who are tracking close behind in a bunched prominent group.

The scrimmage for the prominent slots in the first half-mile is unusually fierce given Maxi Mac Gold, Londonofficecallin, Mister Pink, and Lawful Ruler all want to race forward but cannot all do so — watch for bumping, checked momentum, and early energy expenditure between the 3rd and 6th fences.

Howdoyalikeherhome has a history of jumping errors (PP in recent form) and wears a hood; racing prominently with known fence issues at pace over 2m3½f is a combination worth flagging for in-running safety as well as betting purposes.

Costacurta has finished placed in five straight but has not won since a 19f Good-ground success — watch whether De Bromhead's horse finds a gear at the business end or becomes a consistent second again, as it is the key shape beneficiary if the race runs to type.
